title: Hypertrophy benefits of the Slingshot
summary: NH explains that a slingshot (he uses a Bench Daddy) will not raise a raw bench and deloads the chest at the bottom, but is valuable for bodybuilders with shoulder issues: warming up heavy with it builds confidence and grooves form without fatiguing the chest. He credits it with rehabbing his shoulder injury.
claims: A slingshot adds elastic energy, reinforces tucked elbows and stabilizes the chest so the elbows do not flare out of position
The 2016 slingshot boom was marketing-driven; it does not add 40-60 lb to a raw bench and slingshot benches do not count as raw
The bench is the most frustrating of the big three to progress because it recruits the fewest muscles
Carryover from slingshot bench to raw bench is minimal; raising the raw bench raises the slingshot bench, not the reverse
The slingshot deloads the bottom where the chest and shoulders work most, making it an overload tool for triceps; only slingshot benching for two months could lose you raw strength
Unlike knee wraps, which offload the joint, a slingshot steals tonnage from the chest itself, so replace that chest work elsewhere in the program
His routine: warm up with the slingshot up to 315 lb, then drop to 205-235 lb for paused bench, Spoto press or close grip with no shoulder pain
Much pain is apprehension; moving heavy weight pain-free with the slingshot convinces the brain you will be fine
He hurt his shoulder about two years earlier, thought he would never bench again, and rehabbed it in 4-5 months with the slingshot to full-range pain-free raw benching
Slingshot work leaves the chest fresh for strength work because it mainly tires the triceps, and you rarely fail a bench because of triceps
Use the slingshot with your normal bench form: same elbow flare, touch point and bar path; modify the slingshot if needed
exercises: same form, elbow flare and touch point as raw
shoulder-friendly heavy warm-up, overload for triceps
